name: Religions trivia (easy)
description: 50 easy questions about the world's religions, large and small: beliefs, practices, holidays, history; respectful, no claims about which is true. Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: Which Islamic festival marks the end of the fasting month of Ramadan?
items.explain: Eid al-Fitr, the "Festival of Breaking Fast," celebrates the end of Ramadan.

items.question: How many times each day do devout Muslims perform the ritual prayer known as salat?
items.explain: Salat, one of the Five Pillars of Islam, is performed five times each day.

items.question: To which city do Muslims travel on the hajj pilgrimage?
items.explain: The hajj is the pilgrimage to Mecca in Saudi Arabia, which every adult Muslim who is able must make at least once.

items.question: What is the holy book of Islam?
items.explain: The Quran (also spelled Koran) is the holy book of Islam, which Muslims regard as the word of God.

items.question: On which day of the week do Muslim communities traditionally gather at the mosque for special congregational prayers?
items.explain: Muslim communities gather at the mosque for special prayers on Fridays.

items.question: Which greeting is most commonly exchanged by English speakers at Eid al-Fitr?
items.explain: "Eid Mubarak," meaning "blessed Eid," is the usual greeting for Eid al-Fitr.

items.question: What is the name of the meal Muslims eat after sunset to break their fast during Ramadan?
items.explain: After sunset during Ramadan, Muslims break their fast with prayer and a meal called iftar.

items.question: For how many days does the Jewish festival of Hanukkah last?
items.explain: Hanukkah begins on the 25th of Kislev and lasts eight days, recalling the miracle of the oil.

items.question: Which four-sided spinning top is used in a traditional game of chance at Hanukkah?
items.explain: Playing dreidel, a game of chance with a four-sided top, is a well-known Hanukkah tradition.

items.question: Which leader led the Jewish revolt against the Seleucids whose success Hanukkah commemorates?
items.explain: Hanukkah commemorates the rededication of the Second Temple after the revolt led by Judah Maccabee.

items.question: What event does the Jewish festival of Passover commemorate?
answers: The giving of the Torah at Sinai
The rebuilding of the Second Temple
The Exodus of the Israelites from slavery in Egypt
items.correct: The Exodus of the Israelites from slavery in Egypt
items.explain: Passover commemorates the biblical story of the Exodus and the liberation of the Israelites from slavery in Egypt.

items.question: Which unleavened bread is eaten during Passover?
items.explain: Matzo is specially prepared so the flour does not rise, recalling the haste of the Israelites' departure from Egypt.

items.question: What is the English name for the Jewish holy day of Yom Kippur?
items.explain: Yom Kippur is the Day of Atonement, a solemn day of repentance and fasting.

items.question: Which Jewish holiday marks the start of the Jewish year in the fall?
items.explain: The Jewish year begins in the fall with Rosh Hashanah, which starts the ten-day period ending with Yom Kippur.

items.question: What does the weekly Jewish Sabbath recall?
answers: God resting on the seventh day after creation
The building of the Second Temple
The flood in the days of Noah
items.correct: God resting on the seventh day after creation
items.explain: The Sabbath recalls the seventh day on which God rested after completing creation, as told in Genesis 1.

items.question: What shape is the challah bread traditionally eaten at Rosh Hashanah?
items.explain: Challah at Rosh Hashanah is made round, rather than the usual oval shape.

items.question: What name is given to the first five books of the Hebrew Bible?
items.explain: The Torah is the first five books of the Hebrew Bible, and most Jewish holidays are set out in it.

items.question: Which major Hindu festival is known as the Festival of Lights?
items.explain: Diwali, the Festival of Lights, is one of the major holidays of Hinduism and is also celebrated in Jainism and Sikhism.

items.question: During Diwali, rows of lamps are lit to invite which goddess of good fortune?
items.explain: Lamps are lit at Diwali to ask Lakshmi, the goddess of good fortune, to bring blessings for the coming year.

items.question: How many days after Easter is the Christian Feast of the Ascension celebrated?
items.explain: The Ascension commemorates Jesus rising into heaven on the 40th day after the Resurrection.

items.question: In the Hindu Trimurti, which god is known as the preserver?
items.explain: The Trimurti is the triad of Brahma the creator, Vishnu the preserver, and Shiva the destroyer.

items.question: Unlike many world religions, Jainism does not teach belief in what?
answers: A god who created the world
items.correct: A god who created the world
items.explain: Jainism has no belief in a creator god, though it does teach karma, rebirth and the soul.

items.question: Diwali is often linked to the triumph of Rama over which demon king?
items.explain: Diwali is described as marking the victory of good over evil and the triumph of Rama over the demon king Ravana.

source.title: How Is Diwali Celebrated? Festival of Lights and Beyond

items.question: The Four Noble Truths of Buddhism begin by identifying what as a characteristic of existence?
items.explain: The first of the Four Noble Truths is the truth of suffering (dukkha).

items.question: In Buddhism, what is the state of liberation reached when suffering is ended?
items.explain: The third Noble Truth says that suffering can end, leading to the liberation known as nirvana.

source.title: What are the Four Noble Truths of Buddhism?

items.question: Which spiritual teacher is regarded as the founder of Buddhism?
items.explain: Siddhartha Gautama, known as the Buddha, is regarded as the founder of Buddhism.

items.question: Which of these is one of the major traditions of Buddhism?
items.explain: Buddhism spread across Asia and developed into traditions such as Theravada, Mahayana and Vajrayana.

items.question: Who founded Sikhism in the late 15th century?
items.explain: Sikhism was founded by Guru Nanak, the first of ten Gurus, in the Punjab region.

items.question: Which of these is one of the Five Ks worn by initiated Sikhs?
items.explain: The Five Ks are uncut hair, a comb, short trousers, a ceremonial sword and a steel bracelet (kara).

items.question: Most Sikhs live in which region, home to their holiest shrine, the Golden Temple?
items.explain: Most Sikhs live in the Punjab, where the Golden Temple and the Akal Takht are located.

items.question: What is the Sikh tradition of a communal kitchen serving free meals to all called?
items.explain: The communal meal in the langar is a key Sikh practice that helps break down caste barriers.

items.question: Which Sikh Guru established the Khalsa order in 1699?
items.explain: The Khalsa, the order of initiated Sikhs, was established by Guru Gobind Singh in 1699.

items.question: What is the central scripture of Sikhism, named by the tenth Guru as his successor?
items.explain: Guru Gobind Singh named the Guru Granth Sahib as his successor, and it is the central scripture of Sikhism.

items.question: The word "Sikh" means what?
items.explain: Followers of Sikhism are called Sikhs, meaning "students" or "disciples" of the Guru.

items.question: The word "Christmas" comes from an older phrase meaning what?
items.explain: Christmas derives from Old English Cristes mæsse, meaning "Christ's mass."

items.question: What does Easter Sunday celebrate in Christian belief?
items.explain: Easter Sunday marks the day Jesus rose from the dead, the most significant date in the Christian calendar.

items.question: Which day in Holy Week commemorates the trial and crucifixion of Jesus?
items.explain: Good Friday is the day of Jesus' trial and crucifixion, marked by solemn services in many churches.

items.question: Which Christian holy day, 50 days after Easter, commemorates the descent of the Holy Spirit on the disciples?
items.explain: Pentecost, named from the Greek for "fiftieth," commemorates the descent of the Holy Spirit on Jesus' disciples.

items.question: What is the name of the four-week season of preparation before Christmas?
items.explain: Advent is the four-week period before Christmas, just as Lent is the six-week period before Easter.

items.question: In Shinto, what are the deities or spirits enshrined at shrines called?
items.explain: Shinto shrines are places where the spirit of a deity, or kami, is enshrined or summoned.

items.question: What is the symbolic gateway marking the entrance to a Shinto shrine called?
items.explain: A torii is a symbolic gateway, often painted red, marking the boundary between the ordinary world and the sacred shrine grounds.

source.title: Why do Shinto shrines have torii gates?

items.question: Which of these does Shinto traditionally not have?
items.explain: Shinto has no weekly religious service; people visit shrines at their convenience and on festival occasions.

items.question: What is the central ethical principle of Jainism?
answers: Absolute obedience to a single prophet
Daily sacrifice at a holy fire
Complete devotion to one creator god
items.explain: Jainism's core belief is ahimsa, or noninjury to all living things.

items.question: Who was the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism?
items.explain: Mahavira, who taught nonviolence and asceticism around the 6th century BCE, is counted as the 24th Tirthankara.

items.question: Which ancient sage is traditionally credited with writing the Tao Te Ching?
items.explain: Laozi is traditionally regarded as the author of the Tao-te Ching, the fundamental text of Taoism.

items.question: What does the Chinese word "tao" (or "dao") mean?
items.explain: The Chinese word dao or tao means "way," which gives Daoism its name.

items.question: What is the collection of Confucius's sayings, compiled by his disciples, called in English?
items.explain: The Lunyu, translated as The Analects of Confucius, is the most reliable source of Confucius's teachings.

items.question: In Confucian thought, what is xiao, genuine respect for one's parents, called in English?
items.explain: The Analects explains filial piety (xiao) as genuine respect for parents, not merely providing for them.

items.question: Who founded the Baháʼí Faith in the 19th century?
items.explain: The Baháʼí Faith was founded in the mid-19th century by Baháʼu'lláh, whose name means "Glory of God" in Arabic.

items.question: Which idea is central to the Baháʼí Faith?
answers: Withdrawal from the world into monasteries
The essential unity of all religions
items.correct: The essential unity of all religions
items.explain: The Baháʼí Faith teaches the essential unity of all religions and of humanity, and it has no priesthood.

source.title: Beliefs and practices of the Bahaʾi faith
